stories.teaser: Israeli surgeons are training Zambia’s first pediatric heart team
stories.headline: Israeli heart surgeons are training Zambia’s first pediatric heart team
stories.why: A week in Lusaka: 10 children’s open-heart surgeries, and local doctors mentored to carry on the work.
stories.text:
In Lusaka, a team from Israel’s Save a Child’s Heart performed 10 open-heart surgeries on children in a single week, while mentoring the Zambian doctors who will carry this work forward. Since 1995, the charity has treated 8,500 children from 75 countries and trained 160 doctors and nurses.

“We cannot save the whole world by ourselves,” says surgeon Dr. Hagi Dekel. “So we are training personnel and staff from other countries to repair broken hearts.”

#Israel #SaveAChildsHeart #Zambia #GlobalHealth
stories.og_title: In Zambia, Israeli team helps train country’s first generation of pediatric cardiac surgeons

stories.teaser: Eating with a loved one lowers blood sugar spikes
stories.headline: Eating with a loved one lowers blood sugar spikes, Israeli study finds
stories.why: 339 adults tested at Hebrew University and Sheba Medical Center. Published in Science Advances.
stories.text:
Want a healthier meal? Share it with someone you love.

Researchers at Hebrew University and Sheba Medical Center tested 339 adults and found that people eating with their partner had smaller blood sugar spikes, and returned to normal faster, than when they ate alone. Partners also helped each other cope with cold and stress.

“We actually support each other for basic physiological processes,” says Prof. Shir Atzil.

#Israel #Science #Health #Together
stories.og_title: Blood glucose levels are lower when you eat with a loved one — Israeli study

stories.teaser: Ask kids “how,” not “why,” and 68% think like scientists
stories.headline: Ask kids “how,” not “why,” and 68% think like scientists
stories.why: A Weizmann Institute study of children in grades 2 to 6, published in The Journal of the Learning Sciences.
stories.text:
Your kids may be better scientists than you think.

A Weizmann Institute study of 50 children in grades 2 to 6 found that when asked HOW something works (like how a blowfish puffs up) instead of WHY, 68% came up with plausible scientific explanations. That included second graders.

A small change in how we ask questions can unlock big thinking.

#Israel #Science #Education #Parenting
stories.og_title: Israeli study finds 68% of young kids innately think like scientists
